topic: Matching, transmission lines and the Smith chart

questions.question: Which matching system for Yagi antennas requires the driven element to be insulated from the boom?
What antenna matching system matches coaxial cable to an antenna by connecting the shield to the center of the antenna and the conductor a fraction of a wavelength to one side?
What matching system uses a short length of transmission line connected in parallel with the feed line at or near the feed point?
What is the purpose of the series capacitor in a gamma match?

choices.A: To provide DC isolation between the feed line and the antenna
choices.C: To provide a rejection notch that prevents the radiation of harmonics
choices.D: To transform the antenna impedance to a higher value

questions.question: What Yagi driven element feed point impedance is required to use a beta or hairpin matching system?

choices.A: Capacitive (driven element electrically shorter than 1/2 wavelength)
choices.B: Inductive (driven element electrically longer than 1/2 wavelength)

questions.answer: Capacitive (driven element electrically shorter than 1/2 wavelength)

questions.question: Which of these transmission line impedances would be suitable for constructing a quarter-wave Q-section for matching a 100-ohm feed point impedance to a 50-ohm transmission line?
What parameter describes the interaction of a load and transmission line?
What is a use for a Wilkinson divider?

choices.A: To divide the operating frequency of a transmitter signal so it can be used on a lower frequency band
choices.B: To feed high-impedance antennas from a low-impedance source
choices.C: To divide power equally between two 50-ohm loads while maintaining 50-ohm input impedance
choices.D: To divide the frequency of the input to a counter to increase its frequency range

questions.answer: To divide power equally between two 50-ohm loads while maintaining 50-ohm input impedance

questions.question: Which of the following is used to shunt feed a grounded tower at its base?
What is the purpose of using multiple driven elements connected through phasing lines?

choices.A: To control the antenna’s radiation pattern
choices.B: To prevent harmonic radiation from the transmitter
choices.C: To allow single-band antennas to operate on other bands
choices.D: To create a low-angle radiation pattern

questions.answer: To control the antenna’s radiation pattern

questions.question: What is the velocity factor of a transmission line?

choices.A: The ratio of its characteristic impedance to its termination impedance
choices.B: The ratio of its termination impedance to its characteristic impedance
choices.C: The velocity of a wave in the transmission line multiplied by the velocity of light in a vacuum
choices.D: The velocity of a wave in the transmission line divided by the velocity of light in a vacuum

questions.answer: The velocity of a wave in the transmission line divided by the velocity of light in a vacuum

questions.question: Which of the following has the biggest effect on the velocity factor of a transmission line?
Why is the electrical length of a coaxial cable longer than its physical length?

choices.A: Skin effect is less pronounced in the coaxial cable
choices.B: Skin effect is more pronounced in the coaxial cable
choices.C: Electromagnetic waves move faster in coaxial cable than in air
choices.D: Electromagnetic waves move more slowly in a coaxial cable than in air

questions.answer: Electromagnetic waves move more slowly in a coaxial cable than in air

questions.question: What impedance does a 1/2-wavelength transmission line present to an RF generator when the line is shorted at the far end?

choices.C: The same as the characteristic impedance of the line
choices.D: The same as the output impedance of the RF generator

questions.question: What is microstrip?

choices.A: Special shielding material designed for microwave frequencies
choices.B: Miniature coax used for low power applications
choices.C: Short lengths of coax mounted on printed circuit boards to minimize time delay between microwave circuits
choices.D: Precision printed circuit conductors above a ground plane that provide constant impedance interconnects at microwave frequencies

questions.answer: Precision printed circuit conductors above a ground plane that provide constant impedance interconnects at microwave frequencies

questions.question: What is the approximate physical length of an air-insulated, parallel conductor transmission line that is electrically 1/2 wavelength long at 14.10 MHz?
How does parallel conductor transmission line compare to coaxial cable with a plastic dielectric?
Which of the following is a significant difference between foam dielectric coaxial cable and solid dielectric coaxial cable, assuming all other parameters are the same?

choices.A: Foam dielectric coaxial cable has lower safe maximum operating voltage
choices.B: Foam dielectric coaxial cable has lower loss per unit of length
choices.C: Foam dielectric coaxial cable has higher velocity factor

questions.question: What impedance does a 1/4-wavelength transmission line present to an RF generator when the line is shorted at the far end?

choices.C: The same as the characteristic impedance of the transmission line
choices.D: The same as the generator output impedance

questions.question: What impedance does a 1/8-wavelength transmission line present to an RF generator when the line is shorted at the far end?

choices.B: The same as the characteristic impedance of the line

questions.question: What impedance does a 1/8-wavelength transmission line present to an RF generator when the line is open at the far end?

choices.A: The same as the characteristic impedance of the line

questions.question: What impedance does a 1/4-wavelength transmission line present to an RF generator when the line is open at the far end?

choices.A: The same as the characteristic impedance of the line
choices.B: The same as the input impedance to the generator

questions.question: Which of the following can be calculated using a Smith chart?
What type of coordinate system is used in a Smith chart?
Which of the following is often determined using a Smith chart?

choices.C: Impedance and SWR values in transmission lines
choices.D: Point-to-point propagation reliability as a function of frequency

questions.answer: Impedance and SWR values in transmission lines

questions.question: What are the two families of circles and arcs that make up a Smith chart?
Which of the following is a common use for a Smith chart?

choices.A: Determine the length and position of an impedance matching stub
choices.B: Determine the impedance of a transmission line, given the physical dimensions
choices.C: Determine the gain of an antenna given the physical and electrical parameters
choices.D: Determine the loss/100 feet of a transmission line, given the velocity factor and conductor materials

questions.answer: Determine the length and position of an impedance matching stub

questions.question: On the Smith chart shown in Figure E9-3, what is the name for the large outer circle on which the reactance arcs terminate?
On the Smith chart shown in Figure E9-3, what is the only straight line shown?
How is a Smith chart normalized?

choices.A: Reassign the reactance axis with resistance values
choices.B: Reassign the resistance axis with reactance values
choices.C: Reassign the prime center’s impedance value
choices.D: Reassign the prime center to the reactance axis

questions.answer: Reassign the prime center’s impedance value

questions.question: What third family of circles is often added to a Smith chart during the process of designing impedance matching networks?
What do the arcs on a Smith chart represent?
In what units are the wavelength scales on a Smith chart calibrated?

choices.A: In fractions of transmission line electrical frequency
choices.B: In fractions of transmission line electrical wavelength
choices.C: In fractions of antenna electrical wavelength
choices.D: In fractions of antenna electrical frequency

questions.answer: In fractions of transmission line electrical wavelength
